key_insight: Increasing the barrel filling ratio from 43% to 53% makes detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings denser and more wear-resistant, even though friction slightly increases.
engineering_relevance: This suggests spray-parameter tuning can directly improve protective coating performance for components exposed to severe sliding wear and high-temperature service.
method: Detonation-sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings were deposited at two barrel filling ratios: 43% and 53%.
Microstructure and phases were analyzed by microscopy and X-ray diffraction.
Tribology was tested in dry ball-on-disc sliding at 10 and 15 N and 5 and 10 cm/s.
evidence_signal: The 53% filling-ratio coating showed lower porosity, retained Cr3C2/NiCr as dominant phases with minor Cr7C3 formation, and achieved a minimum wear rate of 1.23 × 10^-4 mm3/(m·N).
watch_item: The improved wear resistance comes with a higher coefficient of friction, so real-world adoption should consider the tradeoff between friction and durability.
paper_title: Effect of Barrel Filling Ratio on the Microstructure, Phase Composition and Tribological Performance of Detonation-Sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr Coatings
